_meta.candidate_policy: Cruising-area research should cover public parks, woods, dunes, beaches, gardens, public toilets, stations, rest/parking areas and comparable publicly accessible spaces. Public toilets in ordinary buildings may be retained as managed-facility leads requiring access review. EXCLUDE dedicated commercial venues and named business-only entries: bars, nightclubs, saunas/bathhouses, gyms, cinemas/theatres, hotels, sex shops, clubs and other fixed nightlife or accommodation venues. Do not add entries back merely because another directory labels a business a 'Cruising Area'. Source frequency counts distinct sites mentioning a place, NOT independently confirmed visits or permission for sexual activity.

cruising_listing_editorial_guidelines.title: Backroom — Cruising Area listing information and writing standard
cruising_listing_editorial_guidelines.scope: Cruising Area listings for open public spaces and publicly accessible facilities, not bars, clubs, saunas, gyms, cinemas, hotels, sex shops or other dedicated commercial venues. Access and legal restrictions must still be verified.

required_content.description: Explain WHERE within the named park, beach, promenade, public area or facility the reported meeting area is: named trails, edges, entrances, sections, landmarks, directions from a recognisable point. Don't merely say 'the park' or 'near the beach' if a more specific location is supported.

When it is reportedly busiest (hours, after sunset, weekends, seasons, after nearby businesses close); distinguish recurring reports from confirmed current hours. Never infer a time simply from the type of place.

Describe, only when supported, the kinds of men reportedly visiting: typical age range, mixed/younger/older crowd, locals/tourists, discreet or social scene and any reported patterns. Do not guess ages or present anecdotal reports as guarantees.

Relevant hazards and cautions: rough rocks/cliffs, water, poorly lit paths, isolated terrain, tide, restricted access, opening hours, crowds/families, privacy, applicable local regulations, closures or changes. Don't invent risks or imply illegal activity is permitted.

Record Latitude and Longitude (numeric decimal degrees) and a usable Google Maps URL, Apple Maps URL and Native Map Query when grounded. Aim for the specific public-area section/entrance described, not merely the city centre or park centroid. Say explicitly when coordinates are only an approximate entrance/reference point. Keep any disputed/unknown coordinates empty and flagged for review rather than fabricating precision.

Write an original, natural and practical friend-to-friend paragraph saying why someone might go, how to find the place, what to expect and concerns. Do not copy source wording or mention internal scraping/extrapolation.

Preserve source URLs and concise notes. Research source-frequency means the number of distinct websites mentioning the location (not the number of repeat exports or pages). Actual verification is separate: count only independent sources that substantively support the precise location and relevant activity, not generic search results or official geography pages. Do not display 'Verified across N sources' just because there are N research mentions.

Use Last_Updated for the date the Backroom listing actually changed, as the master specification requires. Separately track date of latest substantive source verification / report in research notes. Do not confuse Last_Updated with the last time the location was visited. If no recent confirmation is available, disclose uncertainty in internal research status.

gps_and_map_detail.expected_map_behavior: Coordinates should match the described specific subsection or sensible lawful public access point. Both Google and Apple map links must resolve to the correct location; native query should make sense on a smartphone. The map pin must not suggest an arbitrary street/building or another city.
gps_and_map_detail.preferred_accuracy: Exact point or practical public entry for named area if reliable; otherwise public landmark reference point labelled approximate, or leave unfilled if unsupported.
gps_and_map_detail.coordinate_evidence: Cross-check coordinate against place name, geography, source descriptions and map where possible. Preserve differing access-point/meeting-point information as research notes rather than silently choosing an unsupported coordinate.
gps_and_map_detail.privacy_safety: Do not collect or publish real-time locations of individuals, check-ins, private meeting details, user identities or precise private-property access points.
